title: Rookie Actor's Guide
subtitle: Remember, keep the cameras hidden—that's the secret.

items.text: Noire's Set

items.speaker: Crew Member
items.text: Whose is this? It's blocking the camera's sightlines. Get it out of the way!

items.speaker: Extra
items.text: When are we coming in? We've been waiting forever. I wish I brought a chair.

items.speaker: Crowd
items.text: What's going on? Are they filming another movie? Do you see anyone famous?
At the end of the alley, in an old abandoned house filled with camera equipment, crew members and actors go about their business, drawing curious glances from passersby.
One particular figure catches Liáng's attention—someone strangely familiar.
Oh! Is that today's lunch? Mind if I take a look?
Not now? Fine.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: That's that odd person I saw at the hospital. She works for the Foundation.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Who? You mean camera-head over there? What do you mean by odd? You think she could be a fake?

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: No, she's a real Foundation member. I checked her information as well when I inquired about Ms. Noire's file.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Her name is Latham, an Awakened arcanist, currently working in the Arcanum Containment Department.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: I wasn't given any access to her details. But based on our encounter, we should have no problem with her.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Good, fine. I'm happy enough leaving the Awakened to their quirkiness.
She isn't their top priority—Liáng knows that. She pushes aside that odd feeling for now, following Poitier through the crowd and onto the set.

items.speaker: Assistant
items.text: What do you mean she hasn't eaten yet? Director Noire's doctor was explicit that she is not allowed to skip any meals.

items.speaker: Assistant
items.text: Oh, hello, officers. How can I help you?
The well-dressed woman walks over to them.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: We received a call from a Lin Wang. Did you make a report about some unknown person making physical threats and stalking Ms. Noire?

items.speaker: Assistant
items.text: Yes. That's right. I'm Lin, but ...
Upon hearing their purpose, Lin hesitates, glancing uncertainly over at one end of the set.

items.speaker: Actor I
items.text: We did it!

items.speaker: Actor II
items.text: Abby?! You're here!

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: Cut.
At this single command, the actors freeze in place.

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: No. I'm afraid we'll have to roll that again.

items.speaker: Actor II
items.text: I-I'm sorry, director.
The young actor's body stiffens instantly. Based on where he's standing, it's clear that he is only a background character in this scene.
But Noire, seated on her throne-like wheelchair—the overseer of everything—didn't miss his mistake, no matter how minor it was.

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: Not at all. I just want more emotion this time. She's your true love, but you have been apart for a long time. Things are different now. She is, you are.

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: Your reunion must be more complex. It isn't simply happiness you feel. You must mix that emotion with worry and guilt.

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: She doesn't know anything about what happened to you. You can't help but worry that she will never be able to understand you. You wonder if she has got herself into any troubles.

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: I know this is a short scene, but the audience must see your full range of emotions. You are capable of more, so be more.

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: I know you attended drama school, so let's see that training shine. I know you can do it.

items.speaker: Actor II
items.text: Yes, director. I'll try my best.
Simply being noticed by the famous director is enough to leave him visibly flustered. He immediately straightens up, shedding his nervous stance from moments before.

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: Good. Let's roll it again.

items.speaker: Assistant
items.text: Ahem, excuse me, Director Noire?
Seizing this moment before the next take, the assistant swoops in and whispers something to Noire.
Noire glances toward the two officers, her face betraying no emotion. It's impossible to tell what she's thinking.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Huh, for someone that famous, you'd think I'd have known she uses a wheelchair.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: How you feeling? Finally getting a chance to meet your favorite director. Thrilled?
Poitier nudges Liáng with her elbow, tilting forward a little as she teases her. But when she sees Liáng's face, she pauses.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: What's with the long face, kid? Where'd all your excitement go?

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Oh. Is it about the message you got?

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Yes. It's just something that's bothering me.
Before Liáng can explain, the subject of their discussion rolls toward them in her wheelchair.

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: Thanks for coming, officers. But I believe I've already explained that this was all just a misunderstanding.

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: As you can see, I'm in perfect health, well, ignoring these two.
She pats her legs with a cheerful laugh. It seems the director has no qualms about her physical condition, though it's hardly the kind of joke anyone else can comfortably laugh along to.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: But according to your assistant, there's been someone stalking you for months, and they've recently sent you a threatening letter.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: So what—that all just "misunderstandings" too?

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: I'm terribly sorry for inconveniencing you, officers. Lin is a very dedicated assistant, always looking out for me. She may have just overreacted to my situation.

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: I don't mean to brag, but I've been in the limelight for long enough that I've seen my share of crazy fans.

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: I'm used to it.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Sure, I get that. But about that letter you received, do you still have it?
Noire lets out a wry chuckle and shakes her head.

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: I'm afraid I don't have it anymore.

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: I receive so many letters, most of them friendly, some of them not-so-much friendly.

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: I've made a name in this industry, and a few enemies too. If I paid any attention to the negativity, it'd only drag me down. I tend not to keep the bad ones around.

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: While I'm sure you would do a fine job keeping me safe, officers, I can't let myself worry over it. Besides, what are they going to do? Break my kneecaps?

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: Frankly, the only thing I am worried about is that your presence is another distraction for my crew.
She casts a grateful, and perhaps apologetic, look around the set.

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: So, it's very much appreciated that you went out of your way to check in on me, but I have a movie to make. I can't disappoint my fans.

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: Now, if you'll excuse me, we're burning daylight, and I still have four more scenes to film.

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: These Hollywood producers may have opened doors for me, but they also give me so many problems lately.
She smiles at the officers, as if to signal the conversation's end.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Is this really just because of your movie?
Noire has already begun to turn her wheelchair away, but Liáng stops her in her tracks.

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: Pardon me?

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: You seem to be refusing our assistance because you've decided this threat is only a harmless prank.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: You've decided that it's worth the risk to focus on your film.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: I don't mean to judge your decision. It may be understandable in some cases.
She moves closer, lowering her voice as she leans in to deliver the next sentence in a hushed voice.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: But if this threat is not just a prank, if it is serious ...

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: Am I sensing disapproval?
Noire narrows her eyes a little and raises a hand to halt her approaching assistant.
This is a good sign. Liáng has earned the chance to talk for at least a little longer. She pushes aside her conflicting emotions and carries on in a voice only the two of them can hear.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: There has been an increase in patients coming from Chinatown showing signs of mental instability.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Their symptoms include confusion, amnesia, drowsiness, and volatile anger. None of the patients seem to have anything in common. No prior history, all without clear cause.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Does that sound familiar?

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: Sorry, is this leading somewhere?
After a moment of thought, Noire shakes her head, her calm face carrying a perfectly measured hint of confusion.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: A case, eight years ago.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Hé Rìjūn, the scriptwriter for your first big hit, Detective C07. She burned to death in her own house.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: However, the cleaners found a film reel in the debris, surprisingly intact after the fire.
Liáng has been watching Noire's every expression. She doesn't miss the fleeting shift in her eyes at the mention of the film reel.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Strange, isn't it? Every other item was burned to ash, yet this one 8mm reel was as good as new.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: The cleaners felt the same way, so, being curious, they played the reel.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Three of the five who watched it ended up in an asylum, one jumped from a building, and the last, according to the reports, became like an empty shell of a person.

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: And what's happening here reminds you of that?

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: There are some commonalities between the cases. I can't ignore the possibility that they're related.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Two in particular stand out to me, the similar symptoms of those affected, and you.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Hard to shake the thought that these are not coincidences.
Whispers spark among the crew as they eye this secret conversation.

items.speaker: Extra
items.text: What are the police still here for? Are we gonna get back to filming?

items.speaker: Crew Member
items.text: Who knows, but it doesn't seem good. We're losing light here. Can these guys wrap it up already?
These murmurs, of course, don't escape Noire's and Liáng's notice. When she speaks again, Noire's tone is far more direct.

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: Is that an accusation?

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: No, not at all. I'm just hoping you might be able to shed some light on our case.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: After our initial investigation, we officially recorded it as an ominous arcanum incident, and determined that the cause was that 8mm film reel, which contained a film titled Reunion of the Three Swallows.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: To this day, however, the exact nature of the arcanum hasn't been conclusively determined. We still aren't sure why it has this strange effect on people's minds, nor why the damage appears to be irreversible.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Perhaps more importantly, we still don't know the origin behind the arcanum on the reel. There are many possible causes that might create such an effect.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: One of the most common thoughts is from absorbing powerful emotions from an arcanist.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: The darkest emotions possess the strongest power, anger, hatred ...

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Emotions so strong that they can outlast their bearer's death, like a curse from beyond the grave carrying out their last will as an obsession.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: And in such cases, these objects are sure to lead to disaster.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: I believe that this film is, undoubtedly, one such cursed item.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: If it is the case that this film was involved in these new incidents, then we must find out what obsession it's carrying out, and find a countermeasure.

items.speaker: Noire
items.text: I assume you're already on the case.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Indeed, I am, Ms. Noire. I've been studying the report on the original case, including some of the theories of the original investigator.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: One of those theories suggests that despite your collaboration on the C07 series, there were many points of conflict between you and Ms. Hé.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: In fact, the reports mention you had a violent quarrel with her on the day of the fire. There was even a question about whether you might have been responsible for her death.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: So, as you can see, I have more than a strong reason to believe you are connected. And if this cursed reel is behind these recent incidents ...

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: I'm afraid that you may be the intended target of this curse.
